requirements_summary: Dedicated capacity evaluation with heavy emphasis on predictable spend. They want strict customer-configured autoscaling bounds (min/max) as a contractual guardrail. Must have clear behavior when max is reached (throttle vs queue; customer-visible warnings) and an audit trail of scaling decisions + config changes (who/when/why). Prefer VPC deployment (or Private option) due to data governance. They flagged prior incidents with reactive-only autoscaling: latency spikes during ramp-up and unexpected spend during bursty periods.
workload_notes: Mix of summarization + internal knowledge search (embeddings/rerank) and a support-agent workflow used by internal ops teams. Expect predictable weekday diurnal pattern with occasional event-driven spikes (quarter-end / regulatory deadlines).
latency_throughput_targets: Not fully pinned. Directional: interactive flows want p95 latency stability; they care more about avoiding sudden tail spikes than absolute minimum latency. Throughput goal discussed as maintaining steady capacity for baseline + controlled burst to max during events.
autoscaling_success_criteria: 1) Hard max enforcement: spend must not exceed customer max. 2) Min floor honored for baseline traffic to protect SLOs (with documented exceptions during maintenance/drains). 3) Reduced ramp-up latency spikes via pre-scale/predictive signals when confidence is high. 4) Auditability: scaling event history + clamp reasons + config change history, exportable for compliance review.
key_quotes: "We need a hard ceiling. If something goes weird at 2am, we can't wake up to a massive GPU bill."
"If we set a max and hit it, we should see it clearly in the UI and know whether we're throttling or queueing."
"Min isn't about cost for us—it's about keeping performance steady during normal business hours."
